Ashbelites
ASH-bel-ites
n. (proper name; a family of the tribe of Benjamin)
Hebrew 'Ashbeli, the family-name formed from Ashbel, the second son of Benjamin named at Genesis 46:21 and 1 Chronicles 8:1.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

The Ashbelites appear once: “The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites: of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites: of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites” (Numbers 26:38). Benjamin was the youngest of Jacob's twelve and the only one born in the land of promise, and his tribe would be the smallest, the most nearly destroyed, and the most remarkably preserved. The book of Judges closes with Benjamin reduced to six hundred men after the outrage at Gibeah — a tribe within a hair of extinction by its own sin and Israel's sword. Yet out of Benjamin came Israel's first king, and out of Benjamin came the apostle to the Gentiles, who named the tribe when he named himself: “of the tribe of Benjamin” (Romans 11:1). The Ashbelites are one of the houses that carried the tribe through. Their name survives in a census taken before any of that happened, which is the way the genealogies generally work: the families are enrolled, and only later does it become plain which thread God was keeping.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Ashbelites is a Hebrew family-name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Ashbelites is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears once, in Numbers 26:38.

The family descends from Ashbel, a son of Benjamin.

Genesis 46:21 and 1 Chronicles 8:1 both name Ashbel among Benjamin's sons.

The Belaites and Ahiramites are named with them in the same verse.

Key Scripture

Num 26:38 — "The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites: of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites: of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites:"

1Ch 8:1 — "Now Benjamin begat Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third,"

Rom 11:1 — "I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin."

Num 26:53 — "Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names."

Modern Corruption

Tribal lists are treated as retrojected fiction; Scripture uses them to show a preservation no tribe earned.

expand to see more

The twelve-tribe structure is widely handled as a later ideal imposed on a looser reality, with the family lists invented to fill it out. The dictionary holds the lists as record. The test is what the record then does with Benjamin: it tells of the tribe's near-annihilation by its own wickedness, which no inventor flattering a tribal ideal would supply.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is preserving grace. Benjamin was almost cut off and was kept, and the keeping was not for merit — the tribe's great hour in Judges is its shame. That God brought Saul and then Paul out of so nearly extinguished a house is the pattern of His dealing with all His people, who are preserved and not self-preserving.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Ashbeli; the family of Ashbel, second son of Benjamin, enrolled in the census of Numbers 26.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Ashbeli, a family-name formed from the personal name Ashbel.

Ashbel is named second among Benjamin's sons in 1 Chronicles 8:1.

Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son and the only one born in the land.

Numbers 26:41 totals Benjamin at forty and five thousand six hundred.

Judges 20 records the tribe reduced to six hundred men.

Usage

"Benjamin begat Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second"
